title: First Moves: Corners and Urgency
intro: For your first full game, start near a corner. Do not play the first line early: it has no room to breathe or grow.
Make nearby stones help each other. If a stone is in atari, or a cut is urgent, that comes before opening plans.
Here is why corners are a useful beginning. Three walls, three times: count what the board gives you for free.

steps.instruction: Choose a useful first move: near a corner, not on the edge.
steps.hint: The four points a short step in from each corner are all good beginner starts.
steps.explanation: Good. It has room to extend, and the nearby edges can become two walls later. It is a plan, not a promise: answer an urgent atari or cut first.

steps.instruction: That white stone on the first line is an early mistake: choose a stronger opening point instead.
steps.hint: Leave the first line alone for now. Pick a point near a corner with room on both sides.
steps.explanation: Exactly. First-line stones have very little room to make territory. Later, they can matter for saving a group or finishing a boundary; opening priorities are not emergencies.

steps.instruction: A corner wall, one stone short. Finish it -- the gap is on the top edge. Corners are an efficient place to begin.
steps.hint: Top edge, fourth line in from the left.
steps.explanation: Nine points of corner, for SEVEN stones. Two sides of that box were the edge of the board, and the board does not charge you for them.

steps.instruction: The same nine points, but out on the side now. One stone short again -- close the bottom corner of the wall.
steps.hint: The bottom right of the wall you can see, on the fourth column.
steps.explanation: Nine points again -- for ELEVEN stones. Only one side of the box was free this time, so you paid for the extra wall yourself.

steps.instruction: And the same nine points in the open centre. Close the ring.
steps.hint: The bottom right corner of the ring.
steps.explanation: Nine points -- for SIXTEEN stones. Seven in the corner, eleven on the side, sixteen in the middle, for exactly the same territory.

outro: So: open near a corner, avoid the first line early, and make nearby stones work together. When a stone is in atari or a cut is open, answer that urgent problem first.
Corners, sides, influence, and the whole board can wait for Hana's class. For now, this is enough to start a real game.
